nodes.label: Average-Case vs Expected-Case
nodes.rationale: Randomness converts a promise about your input into a promise about your coin flips — and you control the coins. Average-case quantifies over an assumed input distribution the adversary is not drawing from; expected-case quantifies over the algorithm's own randomness and holds on EVERY input.

nodes.label: Las Vegas vs Monte Carlo
nodes.rationale: Las Vegas: always correct, random runtime — the guarantee is on expected time. Monte Carlo: always fast, may be wrong with bounded probability — the guarantee is on the error rate, and errors are independent per run so k rounds give eps^k.

nodes.label: Fisher-Yates Shuffle
nodes.rationale: j must be drawn from 0..=i so the path count is exactly n! and the mapping to permutations is a bijection. The naive 0..n version has n^n paths onto n! permutations — for n=4 that is 256 over 24, so uniformity is ARITHMETICALLY impossible regardless of RNG quality. Measured: -24.83%..+40.37% skew vs Fisher-Yates' +/-0.72%.

nodes.label: Reservoir Sampling
nodes.rationale: Item i enters with probability k/(i+1) and survivors' probabilities telescope to exactly k/n. Theta(k) memory regardless of stream length, one pass — the standard tool for sampling logs, cursors, and telemetry.

nodes.label: Randomness Replaces Balance Logic
nodes.rationale: A treap maintains balance with a random priority per node instead of rotation-counting case analysis (~20 lines vs red-black's); a skip list replaces rebalancing with coin flips and is far easier to make lock-free. You trade a worst-case guarantee for expected behaviour and get a large reduction in code complexity.

nodes.label: CSPRNG vs Fast PRNG
nodes.rationale: Non-cryptographic PRNGs are designed for statistical quality, not unpredictability — xorshift's full state is recoverable from a handful of outputs and a timestamp seed has ~2^30 realistic values. Nothing in the type system marks this, so the rule is per-use-site: OsRng/getrandom for tokens, nonces, keys, salts.

nodes.label: Modulo Bias in Range Generation
nodes.rationale: The same counting argument as the biased shuffle: you cannot partition 2^64 equally-likely values into n equal groups unless n divides 2^64. gen_range uses rejection sampling (or Lemire's multiply-shift); hand-rolled % n does not.

nodes.label: Seed Reproducibility in Tests and Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Randomness is a hidden input: a test's outcome depends on it as much as on the code, so an unrecorded failing run is unreconstructible. Seed with StdRng::seed_from_u64 and print the seed on failure; proptest persists failing seeds automatically, giving exploration and reproducibility together.

nodes.label: Error Amplification by Repetition
nodes.rationale: Repeating a Monte Carlo algorithm with FRESH randomness drives error down exponentially: Miller-Rabin's 1/4 per round becomes 4^-k, and 40 rounds is ~10^-24 — below the probability of a cosmic-ray bit flip.
